content: The University of Bradford is located in Bradford, West Yorkshire, United Kingdom. It originated from the Bradford Schools of Weaving, Design, and Building, which became the Bradford Technical College in 1882. In 1957, it transitioned into the Bradford Institute of Technology, and in 1966, it was granted a Charter of Incorporation, officially becoming the University of Bradford. In 1996, the university merged with the former Bradford and Airedale College of Health, which became the School of Health Studies. The Department of Physics was closed in the 1980s. The 2001 Bradford Race Riots caused a significant decline in university applications, but by 2005, undergraduate applications from domestic students had increased by 35% compared to the previous year. In 2003, a proposed merger with Bradford College aimed to create a combined further and higher education institution. However, the plan was abandoned due to disputes over the new institution's name, which would have required a new charter. The two institutions resumed their competitive and cooperative relationship. In 2004, the university introduced courses in Law and Human Resource Management, directly competing with Bradford College. Consequently, Bradford College sought degree validation from Leeds Metropolitan University in 2005, becoming an associate college of that institution. Approximately 94% of the university's students come from the state sector, with international students comprising most of the remaining 6%. The university announced a £79 million campus redevelopment in 2005, including new residence halls, sports facilities, and a cancer therapeutics research center. Shearbridge Halls were closed and demolished in December 2006. The Richmond Building underwent internal refurbishment and external resurfacing, with a new atrium opening in October 2006. The university became a Fairtrade University in December 2006. The current Chancellor is Imran Khan, a former world-class cricketer and politician, who was installed on December 7, 2005. He succeeded Baroness Lockwood, who served from 1997 to 2005. Previous Chancellors include Trevor Holdsworth (1992–1997), John Harvey-Jones (1986–1991), and Harold Wilson (1966–1985), later Lord Wilson of Rievaulx. The Vice-Chancellor as of June 1, 2007, is Professor Mark Cleary, who joined from the University of Plymouth, where he was Acting Vice-Chancellor (Academic). His appointment was delayed due to the sudden death of Professor Roland Levinsky, Plymouth's Vice-Chancellor. Professor Cleary succeeded Professor Chris Taylor, who retired on April 30, 2007, after serving since October 1, 2001. Professor Taylor had taken over from Professor Colin Bell, who served as Vice-Chancellor from 1998 to 2001 and later held the same position at the University of Stirling. Professor Bell passed away in April 2003, and the University of Bradford now holds an annual memorial lecture in his name, focusing on widening participation. The university comprises seven schools: 1. Engineering, Design, and Technology 2. Health Studies: Formerly the Bradford and Airedale College of Health, it became part of the university in 1996. It specializes in nursing, physiotherapy, midwifery, and radiography courses, as well as a specialist drug therapy course. The department's student body is predominantly female, with a significant proportion of mature students. 3. Informatics: This school includes the Departments of Computing and Electronic Imaging and Media Communications (EIMC). It offers over 40 undergraduate and postgraduate degrees in areas such as computing, ICT, cybernetics, robotics, and media. The school has a strong research culture, with over 100 students pursuing MPhil/PhD degrees. The Department of Computing was one of the first in the UK to offer an MSc in Computing in 1967, with undergraduate courses starting in 1970. The EIMC department, established in 1991, developed its courses in collaboration with the National Media Museum and other institutions. The school has a Digital Arts Centre and a motion capture system used for teaching, student projects, and commercial animation. The school was renamed Informatics when Computing merged with EIMC. 4. Lifelong Education and Development: This school focuses on part-time and specialist degrees in areas such as community regeneration and social studies. It also offers a Combined Studies degree and has been recognized for its research and teaching in Local and Regional Studies. 5. Life Sciences: This school has the largest student body within the university, with over 2,000 students enrolled in courses such as Biomedical Sciences, Chemical and Forensic Sciences, Clinical Sciences, Optometry, Pharmacy, and Archaeological, Geographical, and Environmental Sciences. The school is led by Professor David Coates and has over 100 academic staff actively involved in research. The Bradford School of Pharmacy has developed successful spin-off companies and established the Institute of Pharmaceutical Innovation. The Division of Optometry operates an Eye Clinic providing primary care and student training. The Division of Chemical and Forensic Sciences collaborates with Biomedical Sciences to offer forensic science courses. The Division of Clinical Sciences offers a degree with the option to transfer to Leeds Medical School. The Institute of Cancer Therapeutics conducts high-caliber research and collaborates closely with other divisions. 6. Management: The Bradford School of Management is located on a 13-acre parkland campus three miles from the main campus. It offers undergraduate and postgraduate courses in business, finance, accountancy, management, and marketing. The school is a leading European business school, regularly appearing in top league tables. It collaborates with large corporations and small businesses, providing management development, MBAs, and research opportunities. The school has high employment rates for its graduates and is accredited by prestigious organizations such as EQUIS and the Association of MBAs. 7. Social and International Studies: This school focuses on research-informed education and applied contributions to social and economic issues. It offers courses in social sciences and humanities and hosts the internationally renowned Bradford Centre for International Development and the Department of Peace Studies. The school has a strong focus on international issues and is actively engaged in supporting the local and regional community through initiatives such as the Programme for a Peaceful City. The university's motto, Making Knowledge Work, reflects its focus on employment-oriented courses. It was ranked second in the UK for graduate employment by The Times University Guide in 2005. The official coat of arms bears the motto Give Invention Light, taken from Shakespeare's Sonnet 38. The university has also used slogans such as Be Inspired and Confronting Inequality, Celebrating Diversity in promotional materials. In March 2006, four Bradford students were arrested under the Terrorism Act 2000 on suspicion of terrorism-related offenses. In 2007, they were found guilty of possessing material for terrorist purposes. The University of Bradford Union represents and supports its student body. Notable alumni include Rinchinnyamyn Amarjargal, former Prime Minister of Mongolia, and Nicholas Baines, Bishop of Croydon.
